messages:
sasha: Hey team, customer's dedicated pool failed to scale during a traffic spike this morning — they saw ~30% 5xx and heavy 429s between 10:42–10:48 UTC. They say min_replicas=2, target burst needed ~8, but pool stayed at 2. Request IDs: r-8a3f,r-8a44. Logs show 'scale_up_intent' but then 'node_provision_failed'.

maya: Thanks Sasha. Which cluster/region and customer org? Can you paste the short logs? I'll open a support ticket if it's infra. :eyes:

sasha: org=acme-analytics, cluster=dedicated-eu-west-1-a, model=gptj-8b, region=eu-west-1. Short log snippet from their request proxy: 

```
[2026-03-15T10:42:12Z] INFO scale_decision: desired_replicas=8 current_replicas=2
[2026-03-15T10:42:13Z] WARN provisioner: request_instance -> api_error: quotaExceeded: Insufficient quota for nvidia-a100 in eu-west-1 (sku 'gpu-1').
[2026-03-15T10:42:13Z] ERROR node_provision_failed: last_err="quotaExceeded" retrying
[2026-03-15T10:44:00Z] INFO autoscaler: fallback_to_burst_pool=false reason="billing_soft_limit"
[2026-03-15T10:45:01Z] INFO queue: queued_requests=142 header=X-Req-Queue
```

sasha: They also reported a billing notification earlier: "billing cap reached for dedicated-acme" at 10:40 UTC. Not sure if that prevented scaling.

kai: Interesting, could be multiple failures: cloud quota + billing cap. I'll check cloud quota history for acme. One quick thing — sometimes IAM perms on the cluster service account cause provisioning calls to fail with a different error, but the logs look like quota.

dave: Can you confirm whether the autoscaler attempted any soft-fallback (spot vs on-demand) or used preemptible pools? The snippet 'fallback_to_burst_pool=false' is new; we added that guard a month ago to avoid overspend. If billing cap was on, autoscaler intentionally refuses burst.

maya: Action plan: 1) Kai check cloud quota and raise if needed. 2) Dave check autoscaler decision graph + why burst_pool blocked. 3) I'll confirm billing cap with account team and escalate to customer.

kai: Checked quick console: acme-analytics had A100 quota at 0-> requested increase pending, but there was also an auto-limit on the project: 'soft_quota_override' set to 0 as of 2026-03-15T09:30 — looks like we never approved their increase. Sending request to cloud support now.

kai: Also ran a diff on provisioning errors from our infra logs, found repeated 403/permission-denied for the attach role just before quota error in some attempts: 

```
E0321 10:42:12.845 attach-controller: createInstance failed: iam:CreateInstance: AccessDenied
E0321 10:42:12.846 attach-controller: fallback -> provision attempt aborted
```

kai: So two separate root causes seen: 1) quotaExceeded 2) intermittent IAM attach failures for that customer project. Need both fixed.

sasha: Ugh, customer-facing impact. They already pinged their account rep. Any immediate workaround we can offer them (hotfix) while infra requests are in flight?

dave: Short-term workarounds: 
- Temporarily increase min_replicas to 4 to give more headroom (only helps if nodes can provision)
- Enable burst_pool=true for their dedicated config (requires account approval because of spend risk)
- If quota is the blocker, recommend they request quota from cloud + we help with escalation ID.

dave: Also adding a quick repro to simulate load locally so we can reproduce autoscaler behavior: 

```
# run 30 concurrent requests to customer's dedicated endpoint
for i in {1..30}; do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer x_cust_token" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/dedicated/acme-analytics/generate -d '{"prompt":"test","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
```

maya: I'm going to confirm billing cap with account team. @account-bot can you pull the billing cap for acme-analytics?

account-bot: Billing cap for org acme-analytics: soft_limit=USD 1,000/day, current_spend_today=USD 1,023, soft_limit_enforced=true. Billing notification sent 2026-03-15T10:39:52Z.

maya: Ok that explains 'billing_soft_limit'. Can we temporarily lift the soft_limit for 30 minutes to let them recover? Account team needs confirmation. @dave is it safe to allow burst_pool if quota is still 0? Might still fail.

dave: If quota remains 0, enabling burst_pool won't help for A100 SKUs. But if we switch to a compatible model variant that can run on gpus with available quota (e.g., V100 or T4 quantized) we could help them degrade gracefully. Suggest: offer immediate mitigation by routing new heavy traffic to hosted fallback model (lower perf but available) using routing policy.

sasha: Customer wants timeline. Can we give an ETA?

kai: I'm on quota ticket escalation now. Cloud support responded with priority P2 and asked for org id + request id. I filed that at 10:58 UTC. If they approve fast, nodes could be provisioned in ~15–30m after quota grant. IAM attach failures need devs to confirm service account roles; I will collect exact failing request IDs and attach them to the ticket.

dave: I'll instrument autoscaler to emit a clearer event for 'blocked_by_billing' vs 'blocked_by_quota' and backfill logs for this incident. Short term ETA: 1–2 hours for full remediation (quota + account lift + role fix). Workaround ETA: route traffic to hosted fallback ~15m if account team approves.

maya: I'll message the customer with that plan: explain causes (quota + billing cap + intermittent IAM attach), offer hosted fallback + request to lift soft_limit, and ask if they're ok with reducing model size temporarily.

sasha: Thanks. Please include these repro steps and the two example request IDs in the support ticket. I'll mark this P1 for the customer. :pray:

deploy-bot: Incident draft created: INC-2026-0315-001 (P1) — assigned to support oncall and infra.

maya: Assigning to @kai and @dave. I'll follow up with account team.

kai: I attached the cloud ticket number and logs to the incident: cloud-TKT-99221. Will update when quota status changes.

dave: After this stabilizes, let's add an automated preflight check that validates quotas and billing cap before allowing traffic ramp for dedicated customers. Might prevent surprises.

sasha: Agreed. Closing loop once customer confirms they're back to normal. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
